facts.statement: The genus name Bathyspondylus combines the Greek words for 'deep' and 'vertebra'.
facts.quote: The genus name Bathyspondylus is a compound of two Greek roots: βαθυς (bathys) 'deep' and σπονδυλος (spondylos) 'vertebra'.

facts.statement: The species name swindoniensis honors the town of Swindon where the holotype was found.
facts.quote: The species name B. swindoniensis refers to the town of Swindon in Wiltshire, near which the holotype specimen was discovered.

facts.statement: Bathyspondylus vertebrae featured centra that were set deep relative to the overall length of the bone.
facts.quote: Bathyspondylus had centra set fairly deep in the vertebrae relative to its length, as its name (the Greek words for deep-vertebrae) would suggest.

facts.statement: The vertebrae of Bathyspondylus were short from front to back and had flat or concave ends.
facts.quote: The vertebrae themselves are short antero-posteriorly and can be flat or concave on their terminal faces.

facts.statement: The holotype bones display a mix of features found in both pliosauroids and plesiosauroids.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, from 1774, appears to have features of both pliosauroids and plesiosauroids incorporated into its bones.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, discovered in 1774 at the Great Western Railway Works in Swindon, includes 20 pectoral vertebrae, 23 dorsal vertebrae, one tail vertebra, and various limb bones.
facts.quote: The holotype, DM 1774, which consists of 20 pectoral centra, 23 dorsal centra, 1 caudal centrum, fragmentary neural arches, ribs, ischium, a pubis, complete and broken phalangeals and metacarpals, was discovered in 1774 within the Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian)-aged Kimmeridge Clay Formation within an outcrop located at the Great Western Railway Works in Swindon, England.

facts.statement: The species was formally named and described by J. B. Delair in 1982.
facts.quote: Bathyspondylus swindonensis was named and described in 1982 by J. B. Delair.

facts.statement: Bathyspondylus lived during the Kimmeridgian stage of the Jurassic, approximately 155 to 150 million years ago.
facts.quote: Bathyspondylus lived during the Kimmeridgian faunal stage of the Jurassic period, which occurred roughly 155 to 150 million years ago.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence dates Bathyspondylus to the Kimmeridgian stage between 154.8 and 149.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Kimmeridgian (154.8 to 149.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Paleontologists are unsure of the family classification for Bathyspondylus because it is known only from a few vertebrae.
facts.quote: Because it is known only from its fossil vertebrae (and so few of those have been recovered), paleontologists are not entirely sure of the taxonomy of Bathyspondylus; the family it belongs to is not currently known.

facts.statement: The family placement of Bathyspondylus is currently listed as incertae sedis (uncertain).
Due to the scarcity of recovered fossils, the specific taxonomic family of Bathyspondylus remains unknown.
facts.quote: Debido a que sólo se conoce por sus vértebras fósiles (y muy pocas de ellas han sido recuperadas), los paleontólogos no están completamente seguros de la taxonomía de Bathyspondylus, y la familia a la que pertenece no se conoce actualmente.
